sentences.text: The National Weather Service in Nashville has a Flood Watch in effect for this address, issued October 8 at 11:25AM CDT and running until October 11 at 7:00AM CDT.
The Weather Prediction Center rates Saturday, Oct 10 as a Slight risk of excessive rainfall here, with no risk area on Thursday or Friday.
On 10 of 118 past days rated Slight, a flood was reported within 10 km of this address; that is a count of past days, not a chance for tomorrow.
The Storm Prediction Center shows no tornado risk area at this point on Thursday or Friday, and no severe-weather risk area on Saturday.
On 5 of 3,067 past days with no SPC tornado risk area, a tornado track passed within 25 miles of this address.
NWS HeatRisk is level 1 of 4 (Minor) for both Friday and Saturday, with no value for Thursday; official alerts are at weather.gov.

flood-record.title: How WPC's flood outlooks have played out at this address
flood-record.origin: Our count of past days: WPC morning Day 1 outlooks (Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive) against NWS flood reports with a known location
flood-record.text:
This is a count of past days, not a forecast. From Oct 1, 2016 to Dec 31, 2025, 3,369 days had a WPC morning Day 1 outlook here. A flood report with a known location within 10 km of this address was filed on 33 of those days.
Days with no risk area: a flood was reported within 10 km on 6 of 2,863 days (0.2%).
Days rated Marginal: a flood was reported within 10 km on 10 of 375 days (2.7%).
Days rated Slight: a flood was reported within 10 km on 10 of 118 days (8.5%).
Days rated Moderate: a flood was reported within 10 km on 7 of 13 days (54%).
Days rated High: 0 such days.
WPC changed what its categories mean on Feb 10, 2022. Counting only days since then:
Days with no risk area: a flood was reported within 10 km on 2 of 1,167 days (0.2%).
Days rated Marginal: a flood was reported within 10 km on 2 of 186 days (1.1%).
Days rated Slight: a flood was reported within 10 km on 2 of 53 days (3.8%).
Days rated Moderate: a flood was reported within 10 km on 4 of 5 days (80%), too few days to say anything firm.
Only reports with a usable location are counted, so these are floods that were reported, not every flood.

story.totalsLine: Across these 10 events the National Weather Service recorded 23 deaths, 282 injuries and $2620.2 million in recorded damage.

sentences.text: The National Weather Service recorded an "historic, long-track, strong EF-3 tornado" that began in western Davidson County on Mar 3, 2020, with $1,090,000,000 in recorded damage.
On May 1, 2010, a flood in Davidson County recorded 10 deaths, with Bluff Road closed because of water covering the road.
On Aug 4, 2010, in your zone, heat index values between 110 and 115 degrees left a couple dozen people hospitalized around Metro Nashville.
A snowfall of two and one half inches on Feb 9, 2011 in your zone led to a combined 272 accidents, including 48 with injuries.
On Oct 31, 2013, in your zone, numerous trees and power lines were blown down across Davidson County, and a 9 year old boy was killed by electrocution.
Major and historic flash flooding on Mar 27, 2021 flooded hundreds of homes and businesses, closed I-24, I-40, and I-440, and brought over 130 water rescues.
On Dec 9, 2023, a strong EF-2 tornado struck the Madison area, destroying multiple mobile homes on Nesbitt Lane, where three fatalities occurred.
Overall, the National Weather Service recorded 1,417 weather events in this area since 2000, including 777 Thunderstorm Wind and 121 Flash Flood events.

SE-882999.title: Tornado, Mar 3, 2020
SE-882999.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-882999.text: Tornado on Mar 3, 2020 in DAVIDSON (county TNC037). Deaths: 2. Injuries: 170. Recorded damage: $1,090,000,000 (about $1090 million).
SE-882999.quote: An historic, long-track, strong EF-3 tornado began in western Davidson County then tracked eastward for over 60 miles through Wilson County into Smith County before lifting, causing 5 deaths and 220 injuries. This tornado touched down west of River Road Pike then moved eastward across Bells Bend, destroying a barn and blowing down numerous trees. The tornado strengthened significantly and widened to 0.65 miles wide as it crossed the Cumberland River into the John C. Tune Airport area, causing strong EF-2 damage to numerous planes, hangers, warehouses, and other buildings from Cockrill Bend Way to Briley Parkway. Around $200 million in damage was reported at John C. Tune Airport alone.

SE-226199.title: Flood, May 1, 2010
SE-226199.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-226199.text: Flood on May 1, 2010 in DAVIDSON (county TNC037). Deaths: 10. Injuries: 0. Recorded damage: $1,500,001,000 (about $1500 million).
SE-226199.quote: At U.S. Highway 431 near the Robertson/Davidson County Line at Sycamore Creek, water was overflowing its banks, resulting in flooding of low lying areas. At least one home and farm was reported to be covered with flood waters. At the time of this report, U.S. Highway 431 was still open, although the water level near the base of the road and bridge was rising fast. No additional information was provided concerning any damage to the road or bridge. Also, flooding was reported along Charlotte Road just west of downtown Nashville by the public. Emergency Manager reported closing of Bluff Road due to water covering the road. Water was reported over Culbertson Road along Mill Creek near Nolensville. This made the road impassible to traffic. On Estes Road, approximately one mile west of Green Hills, a creek was flowing over the road. Depth was estimated at three to six inches.

SE-257487.title: Excessive Heat, Aug 4, 2010
SE-257487.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-257487.text: Excessive Heat on Aug 4, 2010 in Davidson (forecast zone TNZ027, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 0. Injuries: 25. Recorded damage: $100,000.
SE-257487.quote: Afternoon temperatures around 100 degrees and unusually high humidity led to heat index values between 110 and 115 degrees on August 4th. Around Metro Nashville, a couple dozen people were hospitalized suffering from heat exhaustion. Several others were hospitalized suffering from burnt feet. There were no known fatalities. There were numerous reports of damage from the heat including exploding tires on automobiles.

SE-282698.title: Winter Weather, Feb 9, 2011
SE-282698.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-282698.text: Winter Weather on Feb 9, 2011 in Davidson (forecast zone TNZ027, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 0. Injuries: 48. No damage figure was recorded.
SE-282698.quote: Two and one half inches of total snowfall accumulation occurred across the county. A newspaper reported that the Nashville Metro Police Department Officers reported 100 accident as roads quickly became snow covered across the area during the first couple hours of snowfall. In total, the Nashville Metro Police Deaprtment and the Tennessee Highway Patrol reported a combined 272 accidents, including 48 with injuries. Details concerning damage to individual vehicles and damage costs were unknown. This total snowfall accumulation also resulted in closures or postponement of civic engagements across the county for the remainder of that day and night on Wednesday, February 9th, as travel across roads throughout the county became hazardous due to the accumulating snowfall.

SE-480287.title: High Wind, Oct 31, 2013
SE-480287.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-480287.text: High Wind on Oct 31, 2013 in Davidson (forecast zone TNZ027, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 1. Injuries: 0. Recorded damage: $50,000. Recorded magnitude: 52 (EG).
SE-480287.quote: Numerous trees and power lines were blown down across Davidson County, especially during the evening hours, with many blocked roads. The KBNA ASOS measured a peak wind gust of 52 mph around 830 PM CDT. One 9 year old boy was killed by electrocution around 930 PM CDT when he rode his bicycle over a live power line that had been knocked down by a fallen large tree limb. This death occurred in the 500 block of Charles E Davis Boulevard around 1.5 miles southeast of downtown Nashville. Trees were reportedly blown down in Old Hickory, a large tree limb was blown down on power lines in the Charlotte Park area of west Nashville, and a large tree limb was blown down in Sevier Park. Trees were blown down and blocked roads such as Robertson Avenue in west Nashville, Towry Street at Paragon Mills Road in Antioch, and Carter Avenue in east Nashville.

SE-951956.title: Flash Flood, Mar 27, 2021
SE-951956.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-951956.text: Flash Flood on Mar 27, 2021 in DAVIDSON (county TNC037). Deaths: 5. Injuries: 0. Recorded damage: $20,000,000 (about $20 million).
SE-951956.quote: Major and historic flash flooding affected southern and eastern Davidson County, with the worst flooding affecting areas along and near Sevenmile Creek and Mill Creek in south Nashville. Hundreds of homes and businesses were flooded, numerous roadways were flooded and closed including I-24, I-40, and I-440, and over 130 water rescues were conducted from people stranded in flooded vehicles and homes. Homes and businesses that were flooded included a hotel at 95 Wallace Road near I-24 at Harding Place, the South Brooke Apartments on Linbar Drive, many homes around Edmondson Pike at Blackman Road, the Walmart on Nolensville Pike at Harding Place with vehicles in the parking lot submerged up to their windows, a home on Truxton Court in Donelson, and the Kroger on Old Hickory Blvd in Hermitage which also had cars stalled in flood waters in the parking lot.

SE-1144554.title: Tornado, Dec 9, 2023
SE-1144554.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-1144554.text: Tornado on Dec 9, 2023 in DAVIDSON (county TNC037). Deaths: 3. Injuries: 21. Recorded damage: $10,000,000 (about $10 million).
SE-1144554.quote: This strong EF-2 tornado touched down just to the east of I-24 on Brick Church Lane in Davidson County. There were a few trees down and shingle damage to several homes in this area. The tornado strengthened in the Madison area causing EF-2 damage with winds up to 120-125 mph. The heaviest damage was confined to two areas, off of East Campbell Road as well as Nesbitt Lane. Multiple mobile homes were destroyed on Nesbitt Lane, and this is where three fatalities occurred. Multiple single family homes and a church off of East Campbell Road were missing large sections of their roofs with some exterior walls collapsed. Several metal power poles in the area were bent as well. Nearby, an apartment complex off Palmer Avenue sustained damage. As the tornado moved further northeast, substantial damage was found to houses in a cul-de-sac on Stoney River Lane.

items.action: The Mar 27, 2021 flash flood in your area affected southern and eastern Davidson County, with 5 deaths recorded. Homeowner's policies do not cover flooding and coverage takes up to 30 days to start, so buy or renew flood insurance well ahead of time.

guidance.text: Purchase flood insurance or renew a flood insurance policy. Homeowner’s insurance policies do not cover flooding. It typically takes up to 30 days for a policy to go into effect, so the time to buy is well before a disaster. Get flood coverage under the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP).

items.action: An EF3 tornado on Mar 3, 2020 passed 0.7 km from this address. Pick your shelter now: a safe room or storm shelter, or otherwise a small interior windowless room or basement on the lowest level, and practice going there.

guidance.text: Identify and practice going to a safe shelter such as a safe room built using FEMA criteria or a storm shelter built to ICC 500 standards. The next best protection is a small, interior, windowless room or basement on the lowest level of a sturdy building.

items.action: A strong EF-2 tornado touched down in Davidson County on Dec 9, 2023, a December event, with 3 deaths recorded in your area. Sign up for your community's warning system and keep NOAA Weather Radio on so alerts reach you at any season.

guidance.text: Sign up for your community’s warning system. The Emergency Alert System (EAS) and NOAA Weather Radio also provide emergency alerts. If your community has sirens, become familiar with the warning tone.
